{{Under construction}}
In 2012{{verify}}<!--2015?-->, [[Robert Jordan]]'s widow, [[Harriet McDougal]], donated a collection of the author's notes to the College of Charleston Special Collections.{{ref|{{Cite/web
 | url=https://findingaids.library.cofc.edu/repositories/2/resources/134
 | title=James Oliver Rigney, Jr., papers, College of Charleston Special Collections
 | date=2015
 | accessdate={{Date|2025 Oct 13}}}}|cofc}} It is housed on the third floor of the Addlestone Library and consists of around seventy boxes of notes covering a variety of subjects. 

The more recent notes relating to plot and character details were used by [[Brandon Sanderson]] to complete the final three books in the series,{{verify}}<!--There are WoBs for this--> although he also used notes that were not part of this collection. The larger set of notes was also used in the creation of [[The Wheel of Time Companion]].

The Addlestone Library collection was used by [[Michael Livingston]] when he was researching his book [[Origins of the Wheel of Time]] in order to put together a history of how The Wheel of Time was written.{{verify}}<!-- Obviously true, but best to point to Origins quote(s) that establish this. -->

==Access==
The collection is mostly available to the public.{{ref|{{Cite/web
 | url=https://findingaids.library.cofc.edu/repositories/2/resources/134
 | title=James Oliver Rigney, Jr., papers, College of Charleston Special Collections
 | section=Access Restrictions
 | date=2015
 | accessdate={{Date|2025 Oct 13}}}}|cofcar}} It is not necessary to book an appointment, but you must present a valid ID. The catalog can be searched and a box requested from the staff. Only one box is permitted in the reading room at a time and only one folder open on the desk at a time. Photos are not permitted, but hand notes can be taken. None of the original notes are allowed to leave the library.{{ref|{{Cite/web
 | url=https://www.reddit.com/r/wheeloftime/comments/181m44f/updated_info_on_checking_out_robert_jordans_notes/
 | title=Updated info on checking out Robert Jordan's notes from the College of Charleston
 | author={{redditor|rilakkumai}}
 | publisher=Reddit
 | date={{Date|2023 Nov 22}}
 | accessdate={{Date|2025 Sep 10}}}}}}

Some materials will not be publicly available until {{Date|2037 Sep 13}}.{{ref||cofcar}}

==Scope==
While the contents of the collection are likely to be of interest to any dedicated fan of ''[[The Wheel of Time]]'' and may be useful in clarifying points of ambiguity within the series and/or providing clarity on what real-world influences affected various WoT terms and choices, the notes should '''not''' generally be thought of as additional canon material. They contain numerous ideas, "facts," notes, etc. that are directly contradicted by the published books and authorial statements. For example, [[Mazrim Taim]] and [[Demandred]] were [[Taimandred|one and the same person]] according to excerpts from Robert Jordan's notes for {{6}},{{ref|[[Taimandred]]|td}} but later published books as well as statements by Jordan and Sanderson directly debunk this theory.{{ref||td}} Therefore, while the notes are of great interest and may be illuminating, they should not generally be used to definitively settle points not established by the books themselves, or at least by clear statements from Jordan and Sanderson. For example, there are notes that support the theory that [[Galad Damodred]] [[Galad Damodred#The Spark|has the spark]], but this should not be taken as absolute proof. Fans should note that Jordan's notes contain such patently non-canon ideas as Nynaeve being evil{{verify}}<!-- Pretty sure this is in Origins --> or Galad being [[Morgase|Morgase's]] lover.{{verify}}<!-- Pretty sure this is in Origins -->

==Organization==
The collection curators have broken the collection down as follows:{{ref||cofc}}
# Biographical material, 1905-2008
# Writings, circa 1979-2009
# Working files, 1980-2009
# Correspondence, 1984-2011
# Marketing and promotional materials, 1980s-2012
# Audiovisual materials, 1991-1995
# Accession 2022-04, 1977-2007

==Media==

The collection contains:{{ref||cofc}}
* DVDs
* Black-and-white photographs
* Clippings (information artifacts)
* Color photographs
* Contracts
* Correspondence
* Files (document groupings)
* Floppy disks
* Galley proofs
* Hardcopies
* Manuscripts for publication
* Notes (documents)
* Printed ephemera
* Promotional materials
* Storage devices (computer equipment)
* Typescripts
* Videocassettes
